findings.title: Null-strategy variants run without the rolling-updates feature that the docs say is required
findings.body: createInitialDeployment returns early when updateStrategy is null, so the rolling-updates feature is only enabled for the RECREATE variant. The operator docs changed in this PR state that while the feature is in preview 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Operator will fail.' Under that statement, the testImageChange-null and testCacheMaxCount-null cases exercise a configuration the docs call invalid, and they still expect rolling/recreate upgrade status. Either the early return should also enable the feature, or the docs claim is wrong and should say the requirement applies only when an update strategy is set.

findings.title: setEnabledFeatures replaces the whole enabled-features list with an immutable List.of
findings.body: The call overwrites any enabled features already set on the FeatureSpec returned by getTestKeycloakDeployment, rather than adding rolling-updates to them, so any feature the base deployment enables is silently dropped for these test cases. Because List.of is immutable, any later code that appends to getEnabledFeatures() on this spec would throw UnsupportedOperationException. Merging into a mutable list would avoid both problems.

findings.title: Changed and new exit codes (3 and 4) are a documented contract but no test asserts them
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3 and FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 is added. The update-compatibility guide presents these exit codes as the interface for CI/DevOps automation. However, UpdateCommandDistTest only checks exit code 0 (testCompatible), and testWrongVersions, which produces the recreate outcome, never asserts the exit code is 3. testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert 4 either. A regression in either code would not be caught, and the renumbering from 4 to 3 is a behavior change that the PR description does not call out.

findings.title: Feature-disabled path is only tested for the metadata subcommand
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled launches only UpdateCompatibility and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata. The equivalent feature gate added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck has no test, so a regression there (for example, the check command running without the feature) would not be caught. The test also asserts only the message, not the exit code 4 that the docs promise.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is documented as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible', which misdescribes a precondition failure
findings.body: Exit code 4 is returned when the rolling-updates feature is disabled and the tool never evaluates the upgrade at all. Describing it as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible' tells automation that the upgrade was assessed and found incompatible. A script that branches on 3 versus 4 could then misread a misconfigured invocation as a real compatibility result. The row should say the command could not run because the feature is disabled.
